headline.text: Satakunta's crude MDT recording share of 0.6% (95% CI 0.2–1.5) lags the 6.0% national benchmark, and a Satakunta study found specialist care caused the biggest diagnostic delay.

details.text: Across overlapping treatment categories where a patient can have several treatments, Satakunta's crude curative share is 24.5% (95% CI 21.4–27.9; n=167/682), whose 95% confidence interval includes 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, while crude symptomatic treatment is 29.0% (95% CI 25.8–32.5; n=198/682) versus 39.5% (5871/14873) and crude life-prolonging treatment is 45.0% (95% CI 41.3–48.8; n=307/682) versus 30.4% (4522/14873), with 95% confidence intervals excluding national values.

Satakunta's crude share of patients with no treatment record within 12 months is 29.8% (95% CI 26.4–33.3; n=203/682) compared with 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, so its 95% confidence interval includes the national value and is not distinguishable from it; this category mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded.

An MDT meeting is recorded for a crude 0.6% (95% CI 0.2–1.5; n=4/682) of Satakunta patients versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, but HILMO procedures are entered only from direct patient contacts, so MDT records measure recording practice rather than care.

A University of Turku regional study of Satakunta found the biggest delay from referral to diagnosis occurred in specialist care, and preliminary, unpublished national figures show 155 days from symptoms to treatment in Finland versus 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark, with 58 days in specialist care, 56 in patient delay, and 41 in primary care.

headline.text: Satakunta's published table figures are crude shares that are not age-adjusted and cannot be stage-adjusted, while public data omit primary care, referrals, and treatment start dates.

details.text: The county table (Taulukko 11) gives crude shares that are not age-adjusted, whereas county-level age-adjusted treatment shares appear only in the report's Kuva 16 PNG figure by sex, where digitised national reference lines for curative treatment are 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women, read from the figure at about ±0.5 percentage points.

Separately from age adjustment, the crude county shares cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients, even though a 2019 Lääkärilehti journal article found that HILMO hospital discharge diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types.

Public report data do not measure symptom onset or referrals, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, and imaging appears only indirectly as diagnosis based on clinical findings alone in about 20% of patients rather than imaging wait times.

The report tracks whether a specialist visit occurred within 12 months (93.6% nationally) and which treatment type was recorded within 12 months, but not when specialist visits or treatments started, while Finland has no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion under the Health Care Act (§52) and no cancer quality registry.

headline.text: The team recommends reporting THL 21/2016 access times with handover alerts, adopting a KYS-style referral template and diagnostic contact person, and publishing county stage, drug, and MDT recording.

details.text: Because a Satakunta regional study found the biggest diagnostic delay in specialist care, the team recommends reporting access times (referral, first specialist visit, diagnosis, and treatment start) using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers and flagging stalled handovers while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

The team recommends adopting a standard referral content list and template modelled on KYS's regional pathway document and a primary-care rule to refer persistent unexplained symptoms for a pulmonologist assessment even after a normal X-ray, as KYS is the only reviewed pathway with these rules and mentor insight notes weak referrals receive lower urgency ratings in specialist care.

The team also recommends naming a contact person for the diagnostic phase from referral to diagnosis because no reviewed regional pathway document names a diagnostic-phase contact, whereas the STM roadmap's measure 1.2.3 plans national guidance on a named care-coordinator model by 2026–2028 and county adoption by 2029–2031 without specifying the care phase.

Given Satakunta's crude recorded MDT share of 0.6% (95% CI 0.2–1.5; n=4/682) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally and about 48% missing stage at diagnosis nationally, the team recommends publishing per-county recording of stage, drug treatment, and MDT meetings and reading county gaps in these fields as data-quality signals alongside the Filha programme's call for uniform recording instructions.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
